items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Had Albert Morgan on bass, me on banjo, and John Robichaud on piano, had David Jones and Theta on sax, and Lee Collins on trumpet.

ctx.x: Budweiser? Was it near the Budweiser?

Well, maybe this was the fern, it was the Budweiser and the fern, they were right next to each other. The Vila was the La Vila? La Vila, that's it, that's it. Yeah. John Maria had charge of that job, and he had... It was his job, John Maria to banjo. Well, like I said, I used to always go around, you see. In fact, I can tell you, there's a different place, they had a different place on St. Charles and Cronolette. They had one on Burgundy and Canal. And then, like you said, the La Vila and the Vila were right next…
Well, they didn't, yeah, that's Astor Strutton.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: Binge got the idea of taking the show and, and building this band with, uh, with Lee Collins and David Jones as the leader of it, see. This, this Binge fellow, he's the guy? Sam Binge, that, you know, that, where we played at Fowler, that place, on Royal Street, yeah, yeah. So, um, we worked there.

ctx.x: You missed out the, uh, the Lee Collins period there. Well, I, well, that, oh, yeah, that's right,

that's right. That was, that was before Sidney Desmond, I mean Sidney Desmond, because there was, there was a fella named John Morell, banjo player. He had a job at the La Vida, as a jitney dance. That's right. And, um, and that band was, the leader was John Morell, the banjo player, and, uh, Lee Collins on trumpet. Thereto Poinnell on alto and David Jones on tenor. Yeah. Uh, Joe Rovershaw on piano, uh, and, uh, Albert Martin, I think, the drummer. Oh, Albert Martin. Yeah. On drum, and I took John Morell's play.…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: Lee Collins, that's when I recorded that thing they called it, Astoria Hot 8.

ctx.x: And you were playing banjo at this time?

At that time I was born for the Stikker Steamboat Company. Uh-huh. And there was a ten piece band. It had three sax, three brass, and four rhythms. And you had to play banjo, you had to play pangeline guitar. If you were bass, you had to play bass following and bass horn. I worked with, I started with Fate Marble, and then they had a job with Sidney Desveen, and that's where he came to me. We used to play at the country club on Sundays. And that's where the Captain Vaughan came in and heard the band and I used to…
Yeah, for about ten years. And that's when you.
